Start With a Name. Leave With a Brand.

Most founders have to hire four suppliers: a designer for the logo, a digitizer for the embroidery file, a patch supplier, and then a factory. Four briefs, four invoices, and artwork that drifts at every handover. We are all four.

How it works

From a name to packed cartons

Six steps, one supplier. You are not briefing four companies and hoping the artwork survives.

You arrive with a name

Sometimes that is genuinely all there is - a name and an idea of who it is for. That is enough to start.

We design the identity

Our designers draw an original logo and the marks that go with it: wordmark, icon, label lockup. Not a template, not AI output - drawn for you, and yours.

We make it production-ready

The logo becomes real production files: vector artwork for print, a digitized stitch file for embroidery, and artwork separated for sublimation. This is the step most brands pay a stranger for and then discover does not run properly.

We make the trims

Woven labels, embroidered, chenille, PVC or leather patches, hang tags. Made here, matched to the artwork that was just drawn, by the people who drew it.

We cut and sew the garments

Your fabric, your weight, your fit, decorated with the files we made. MOQ from 20 pieces, so a first run is a real test and not a gamble.

It ships to you, DDP

Packed, labelled and delivered duty paid, so the quoted price is the landed price.

Why one supplier

What changes when the factory draws it

The digitizer sees the garment

Every other digitizing service emails a file and never finds out what happened to it. Stitch density that works on a 180 gsm jersey tee puckers a 450 gsm fleece, and the only way to know is to sew both. We sew both.

One brief, not four

Artwork drifts every time it changes hands - a colour shifts, a line weight thickens, a logo gets re-traced from a JPEG someone exported badly. Here it never leaves the building.

Fix it before it is stitched, not after

Tiny text, thin strokes and gradients fail in thread. We tell you at the drawing stage, when it costs nothing to change, rather than after 300 hoodies are embroidered.

No minimum to find out

MOQ from 20 pieces on most styles. You can launch one style, see what sells, and reorder.

The services

Everything between a name and a garment

Each is included when you place a production order, and quoted on its own if you only need the file.

Embroidery Digitizing

Your logo turned into a stitch file that runs clean on the machine - programmed by hand, by people who will also be sewing the garment it goes on.

Vector Art & Logo Design

From a blurry JPEG to print-ready vector - or from nothing at all to an original logo drawn for your brand.

Custom Patches & Labels

Embroidered, woven, chenille, PVC and leather - made here, and sewn onto the garments we make for you.

Sublimation Printing

Dye bonded into the fibre, not sitting on top of it - printed on the panel before the garment is sewn, so the graphic runs right to the seam.

On pricing. Artwork, digitizing and vector work are included with a production order. If you want the files on their own, we quote them individually - tell us what you need and we will put it in writing before anything starts.
